name: SBGR
description: Benchmark, optimizers, experiment scripts and campaign data for the study Artificial Bee Colony for Constrained Optimization in 6G-Motivated Analog Integrated Circuit Design: A Surrogate Benchmark and a SKY130 Cross-Check (under review, Applied Soft Computing). SBGR is a deterministic closed-form benchmark that reproduces the optimization structure of bandgap-reference transistor sizing — maximise power-supply rejection subject to six coupled specifications — for fair, reproducible, simulator-independent comparison of constrained metaheuristics. Version 1.3 added the transistor-level cross-check: the same constrained-optimization formulation re-posed against bandgap references in the open-source SkyWater SKY130 process and evaluated with ngspice, over the five bandgap campaigns and 900 runs, 30 paired seed blocks per case. Two campaigns use the current-mode (Banba) core of the motivating reference design, which makes five of its six published specifications applicable verbatim; three use a voltage-mode (Kuijk) core. The measured finding is that an optimizer ranking on this problem is contingent on the specification set, on the core topology and on the evaluator.
